answer.question: What should a Dove Valley business bring to a turf consultation?
answer.answer: The activity, equipment, traffic and schedule, plus delivery access and any operations that must stay open. Confirm the parcel and project with Arapahoe County, since a sports-turf label doesn't establish permission.

blocks.h2: Begin with what happens on the surface.
blocks.takeaway: A field, training lane and play area can need different surfaces, edges and upkeep, so describe the activity and equipment first. Near the airport, plan delivery access and keeping neighboring operations open.
paras: A field, training lane and recreational area can need different surfaces, edges and maintenance. Describe how people move, what equipment they use and the schedule the property needs to maintain. Ask for the proposed system and relevant product documentation before selecting it.
Around Dove Valley’s business and airport area, delivery access and keeping adjoining operations available can be part of the job. Make those constraints visible in the installation discussion.

blocks.h2: Settle planning questions before the final footprint.
blocks.takeaway: Dove Valley is unincorporated, so confirm your project with Arapahoe County — a product labeled sports turf doesn't establish permission for any site on its own. Keep grading, drainage and removal separate in the estimate.
paras: Dove Valley is unincorporated, so confirm the parcel and intended project with Arapahoe County. Commercial and shared-area landscape requirements depend on the type of proposal; a product advertised as sports turf does not establish permission for any site.
For a home yard, bring applicable property requirements and explain how the space will be used. In either case, identify grading, drainage and removal separately in the written estimate.

blocks.h2: Playing fields stay open to turf under Colorado's 2026 rules.
blocks.takeaway: A practice field, training area or playground can still take artificial turf under Colorado's 2026 rules; a decorative lawn outside an office building is what they aim at.
paras: The Denver Broncos' headquarters and training camp, Broncos Park Powered by CommonSpirit, is in Dove Valley (Denver Broncos), and so is most of Centennial Airport. That makes this a place of fields, hangars and business parks as much as homes, and Colorado's turf law treats those very differently.

Since 1 January 2026, local governments can't allow non-functional turf on new commercial, institutional or HOA common-area projects, under SB24-005 and its 2025 amendment, HB25-1113 (SB24-005, HB25-1113). Athletic fields of play were excepted from the start, and playgrounds and sports fields count as functional turf.

So a practice field, a training area or a playground can still take artificial turf, while a decorative lawn outside an office building is the kind of installation the law is aimed at. Our guide to where Colorado draws the functional line has the definitions.

blocks.h2: Flat airport-bench ground over clay that moves.
blocks.takeaway: Front Range clay here can swell up to 20% when wet, and on flat ground a thin base leaves puddles. We grade the site and build a base suited to the clay.
paras: Dove Valley sits around 5,800 feet on the flat to gently sloping bench that holds Centennial Airport. Flat ground helps, because water can be sent off a field or a yard in a controlled way; it also means a thin base leaves puddles standing.

Under it is Front Range clay. The Colorado Geological Survey describes montmorillonite and bentonite clays, along with weathered volcanic ash, that can grow by up to 20% of their volume when they get wet and exert up to 30,000 pounds of pressure on every square foot. Heaved slabs and cracked foundations, driveways and sidewalks are the usual result (Colorado Geological Survey).

The fix is in the preparation. We grade the site, build a base suited to the clay, and lay, seam and edge the turf before the infill goes in, so a field or a yard stays level through wet springs and dry summers.

blocks.h2: Runways, hangars and business parks, with fields and courts between them.
blocks.takeaway: Around the airport's offices and business parks, a play area or a putting green for staff counts as functional turf, not a decorative lawn.
paras: Centennial Airport covers about 1,400 acres, with three asphalt runways and a round-the-clock FAA tower with U.S. Customs, at 5,885 feet. It logged 337,947 aircraft operations in 2018, about 925 a day and 89% of them general aviation, and most of it lies in Dove Valley before it runs into Douglas County (Centennial Airport).

Around it sit the Randy Ross Tennis Center and company headquarters such as Key Lime Air's (Dove Valley). For a business here, the useful question is the one above: functional turf, like a play area or a putting green for staff, or a decorative lawn by the front door.

faq.q: Who installs artificial turf in Dove Valley, CO?
faq.a: We install sports field turf, commercial turf and residential artificial turf in Dove Valley, CO, home of the Broncos' training headquarters and most of Centennial Airport. Under Colorado's 2026 turf rules, sports fields and playgrounds count as functional turf and stay allowed, while decorative lawns on new commercial projects are barred. Call 303-349-2368 for a free estimate.

faq.q: Does an existing turf field in Dove Valley have to come out?
faq.a: No. Commercial and HOA turf from before 2026 is grandfathered, but a redevelopment that disturbs more than half the landscape triggers the ban on non-functional turf (SB24-005). A sports field counts as functional either way, so a worn field can get new turf in place of the old.

faq.q: Is artificial turf allowed in a Dove Valley back yard?
faq.a: Yes, as far as state law goes: Colorado's turf law leaves single-family yards alone. If your home is in an HOA, its design rules can't forbid nonvegetative turf out back at a detached single-family house (SB23-178). Attached homes are treated differently, so send the board your plan and get its answer in writing.

faq.q: Who applies the turf rules in Dove Valley, a city or the county?
faq.a: The county. Dove Valley is unincorporated, so Arapahoe County is the local government that applies the state turf law here. Ask its planning staff how it reads your site before a commercial layout is final.

faq.q: What watering rules apply in Dove Valley?
faq.a: That depends on your provider. Dove Valley is unincorporated and has no city water utility, so the name on your bill tells you whose watering rules you're under. Turf needs no watering schedule at all.

faq.q: Can a rebate help pay for turf in Dove Valley?
faq.a: Not for turf. Resource Central runs the lawn replacement program that Denver Water, Aurora Water and Highlands Ranch Water all take part in; it needs at least 200 square feet of lawn replaced with a landscape of at least 50% waterwise plants, and its 2026 program is full (Resource Central). Our rebates guide covers the rest.
